interactions.summary: Jiang confirms that the marriage vow is spoken aloud and signed in ceremony, then draws the consequence himself: a spoken covenant creates a bond whose violation is not trivial because covenant language carries death-price seriousness.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang with the same responding student

interactions.summary: Jiang sharpens the practical consequence by saying adultery converts a relationship from trust into suspicion, and a student contrasts human relationships with God by arguing that God can see whether inner repentance is real.

claims.claim: The marital vow is not only inwardly intended; it is spoken aloud and signed in a ceremony, which is why Jiang treats it as a real bond rather than a private mood.
Jiang says cheating matters because it breaks the bond created by the vow rather than because sex itself is magically contaminating.
The student intensifies the covenant logic by saying covenant means accepting a death-price for breach, invoking the biblical image of becoming like the animal cut in half.
Jiang's cleanest formulation is that the affair changes the relationship from trust to suspicion; the sex is secondary to the collapse of trust.

A student argues that divine judgment differs from human reconciliation because God can see whether someone has actually become a different person, while a boyfriend or girlfriend can only choose whether to believe the claim.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang strips the issue down to betrayal's real substrate: adultery matters because it destroys trust and installs suspicion.
signature_moments.source_phrase: The sex is not the issue. The affair's the issue. The trust is the issue.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's clearest reusable definition of what the sin actually changes.

signature_moments.moment: The covenant is imagined through the violent biblical image of the body cut in half if the promise is broken.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I shall be like the animal that got cut in half.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives the vow a sacrificial gravity that explains why Jiang refuses to treat marriage promises as cheap speech.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The relational reality created by the spoken vow and then broken by cheating.
A vow structure with life-and-death seriousness, illustrated through biblical sacrificial imagery.
The core relational good Jiang says adultery damages, and the measure human partners cannot perfectly verify once it is broken.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet turns the class from naming the vow to articulating its consequence: covenant creates a bond, adultery converts trust into suspicion, and divine judgment is introduced as the only perfect reader of inner change.
